flagged.evidence: `def-two-design` says: `Let v,k,\lambda be natural numbers with 2\le k<v ... A 2-(v,k,\lambda) design ...`. `def-steiner-systems-and-steiner-triple-systems` says: `A Steiner triple system of order v ... is a 2-(v,3,1) design.` So under the library's own definitions an STS(v) requires `3<v`. But this theorem begins `Let m\in\mathbb N` and concludes a Steiner triple system on `6m+3` points. Taking `m=0` gives `n=1`, point set `(\mathbb Z/1)\times(\mathbb Z/3)` with 3 points, and step 4.1 calls the result a `2-(3n,3,1)` design, i.e. a `2-(3,3,1)` design. That object is excluded by `k<v`. The claim needs the small-order exclusion, e.g. `m\ge1`.

The same dependency texts force `STS(v)` to mean a `2-(v,3,1)` design with `2\le 3<v`, so no Steiner triple system exists for `v=1` or `v=3` in this library. Yet the Statement says `A Steiner triple system of order v exists iff v\equiv1 or 3 mod 6`, and both `v=1` and `v=3` satisfy that congruence. The proof reflects the problem: step 1.2 uses Bose at `v=6m+3`, which includes `v=3` via `m=0`, and step 1.3 explicitly says `v\equiv1 mod6 forces v\ge7`, which is false because `v=1` is a counterexample. The theorem needs a hypothesis excluding the small orders (equivalently `v>3`).
